strings.term.ACTIVE_DL_SLOTS.body: The maximum number of torrents allowed to consume download slots at the same time. Extra started torrents wait in Queued state. Seeding torrents do not consume a download slot. 0 means unlimited.
strings.term.ACTIVE_DL_SLOTS.title: Active Download Slots
strings.term.ACTIVE_TRANSFERS_VIEW.body: The main torrent queue and selected-torrent inspector. Transfers continue running when you switch to Create Torrent or Preferences; changing views does not pause network activity.
strings.term.ACTIVE_TRANSFERS_VIEW.title: Active Transfers
strings.term.APPLICATION_STATE.body: Writable settings, session metadata, cached torrent metainfo, shell-integration backup state and UI error logs. Installed and portable builds deliberately use different state-directory policies.
strings.term.APPLICATION_STATE.title: Application State Directory
strings.term.AUTO_RESUME.body: When enabled, torrents that were actively downloading or seeding at clean shutdown are scheduled to become active again on the next launch. Paused and stopped torrents keep their intentional inactive state.
strings.term.AUTO_RESUME.title: Restore Active Transfers
strings.term.AVAILABILITY.body: An estimate of how many complete copies of the torrent are represented by pieces advertised by connected peers. Below 1.0 can mean the current connected swarm does not contain every piece required to finish.
strings.term.AVAILABILITY.title: Swarm Availability
strings.term.AVERAGE_PEAK.body: Average summarizes the recent retained speed samples; Peak is the highest sample in that retained history. These are session telemetry values, not advertised ISP line speed or theoretical network capacity.
strings.term.AVERAGE_PEAK.title: Average and Peak Transfer Rates
strings.term.BEP.body: A numbered specification describing a BitTorrent protocol or extension. Examples: BEP-5 defines IPv4 DHT, BEP-9 defines magnet metadata exchange, BEP-11 defines Peer Exchange, BEP-14 defines Local Peer Discovery, BEP-15 defines the UDP tracker protocol including scrape, BEP-32 extends DHT to IPv6, and BEP-48 documents HTTP tracker scrape conventions.
strings.term.BEP.title: BEP - BitTorrent Enhancement Proposal
strings.term.BEP32.body: The BitTorrent extension that adds IPv6 node/address forms to the DHT. SalixTorrent maintains separate IPv4 and IPv6 UDP sockets/address spaces and uses family-appropriate n4/n6 node requests without running a duplicate polling loop.
strings.term.BEP32.title: BEP-32 - IPv6 Extension for DHT
strings.term.BEP52.body: Defines BitTorrent v2 metainfo, SHA-256 info hashes, the file tree, per-file pieces roots, piece layers and hash peer messages. SalixTorrent keeps the full SHA-256 identity while using the required 20-byte truncated identity on tracker, DHT and peer-wire surfaces.
strings.term.BEP52.title: BEP-52 - BitTorrent Protocol Specification v2
strings.term.BEP9.body: The protocol used to retrieve a torrent's metadata from peers when you start with only a magnet link. SalixTorrent downloads the metadata in small pieces, reconstructs it, and verifies that its SHA-1 info hash matches the magnet before accepting it.
strings.term.BEP9.title: BEP-9 - Extension for Peers to Send Metadata Files
strings.term.BITTORRENT_V2.body: The second BitTorrent metainfo and peer-protocol generation. v2 uses SHA-256 torrent identity, file-aligned pieces, per-file Merkle trees and piece layers. SalixTorrent validates this Phase-8 foundation and Phase 9 uses it for live v2-only and hybrid swarm networking, hash exchange, magnets and creation.
strings.term.BITTORRENT_V2.title: BitTorrent v2 / BEP-52
strings.term.BLOCK.body: Pieces are normally requested from peers in smaller blocks (commonly 16 KiB). Blocks can arrive out of order or from different peers. A piece is not trusted until all of its blocks are present and its hash verifies.
strings.term.BLOCK.title: Piece Blocks
strings.term.CANCEL_MESSAGE.body: BitTorrent peer-wire message ID 8. A downloader sends CANCEL for a previously issued block REQUEST when that work is no longer needed, such as after another peer wins an endgame race or a request is reassigned. SalixTorrent both sends CANCEL and honours received CANCEL messages for pending uploads.
strings.term.CANCEL_MESSAGE.title: Peer-wire CANCEL Message
strings.term.CGNAT.body: NAT performed by the Internet provider upstream of your own router. With CGNAT, your router may not own a directly reachable public IPv4 address, so a local UPnP or manual port-forward rule may still be unreachable from the Internet. The shared IPv4 range 100.64.0.0/10 is a strong indicator, but absence of that range does not rule CGNAT out.
strings.term.CGNAT.title: CGNAT - Carrier-Grade NAT
strings.term.CLEAN_SIGNAL_SHUTDOWN.body: Ctrl+C, SIGTERM and Windows SIGBREAK request the same centralized TorrentManager shutdown used for ordinary application exit, allowing live peer, tracker, DHT, listener and disk work to close through their normal lifecycle owner.
strings.term.CLEAN_SIGNAL_SHUTDOWN.title: Clean Signal Shutdown
strings.term.CLOSE_TO_TRAY.body: When enabled and supported, the window close button hides SalixTorrent while transfers continue. Tray > Exit always performs a real clean shutdown. If the tray backend is unavailable, Close falls back to normal application exit so the program cannot become invisible and unreachable.
strings.term.CLOSE_TO_TRAY.title: Close Window to System Tray
strings.term.COMPLETION_NOTICE.body: Shows a small SalixTorrent window when a download reaches completion. It can provide a quick Open Folder action without relying on operating-system notification services.
strings.term.COMPLETION_NOTICE.title: In-app Completion Notice
strings.term.CONNECTED_PEERS.body: The number of live BitTorrent peer connections currently attached to this torrent. This is different from the number of peers discovered by trackers, DHT or PEX because not every discovered endpoint connects.
strings.term.CONNECTED_PEERS.title: Connected Peers
strings.term.CONNECTIVITY_ACTION.body: A practical next step based on the latest mapping result. Suggestions may include enabling UPnP/NAT-PMP, choosing another listen port, configuring a manual TCP port forward, checking the active VPN/default route, or investigating double NAT/CGNAT. The wording is guidance, not a claim that SalixTorrent can inspect router settings it cannot see.
strings.term.CONNECTIVITY_ACTION.title: Connectivity Suggested Action
strings.term.COPY_INFO_HASH.body: Copies the selected torrent's canonical info-hash identity. v1 uses SHA-1, v2 uses the full SHA-256 identity, and hybrid torrents carry both identities internally.
strings.term.COPY_INFO_HASH.title: Copy Info Hash
strings.term.COPY_MAGNET.body: Builds and copies a generation-aware magnet URI: btih for v1, btmh for v2, and both compatible exact-topic identities for hybrid torrents, plus display/tracker parameters.
strings.term.COPY_MAGNET.title: Copy Magnet Link
strings.term.CREATED_BY.body: An optional metainfo field identifying the application that created the .torrent. It is descriptive only and does not prove who authored or owns the payload.
strings.term.CREATED_BY.title: Created By
strings.term.CREATE_TORRENT.body: Builds BitTorrent v1, v2 or recommended hybrid .torrent metainfo from an existing file or folder. SalixTorrent hashes the source in the background using the selected generation; the payload itself is not copied merely to create the .torrent file.
strings.term.CREATE_TORRENT.title: Create Torrent
strings.term.CREATION_DATE.body: An optional Unix timestamp stored in the .torrent metadata. It describes when the torrent file was created, not necessarily when the underlying payload files themselves were created.
strings.term.CREATION_DATE.title: Torrent Creation Date
strings.term.CREATION_PROGRESS.body: Shows hashing progress while SalixTorrent reads the source and generates SHA-1 piece hashes. Creation runs in a worker thread so the user interface remains responsive. Cancelling does not replace the destination with a half-written torrent.
strings.term.CREATION_PROGRESS.title: Torrent Creation Progress
strings.term.DEFAULT_DOWNLOAD_DIR.body: The storage root assigned to newly added downloading torrents. Existing torrents remember their own storage paths, so changing this preference does not silently move data that is already in progress.
strings.term.DEFAULT_DOWNLOAD_DIR.title: Default Download Directory
strings.term.DELETE_DATA.body: A destructive cleanup action. It removes the torrent from SalixTorrent and deletes payload data managed under the torrent's download storage, plus resume metadata. External seed sources and the original opened .torrent file are deliberately protected.
strings.term.DELETE_DATA.title: Remove + Delete Data
strings.term.DHT.body: A decentralized BitTorrent peer-discovery network. SalixTorrent participates in the IPv4 BEP-5 DHT and the IPv6 BEP-32 DHT when those address families are available. A specific network bind restricts DHT to that family. Private torrents deliberately disable DHT.
strings.term.DHT.title: DHT - Distributed Hash Table
strings.term.DIAGNOSTICS.body: A support/development snapshot containing version, runtime, selected torrent, discovery settings, connectivity state, desktop tray/notification capabilities and application-data file locations. It is designed to make troubleshooting reproducible.
strings.term.DIAGNOSTICS.title: Diagnostics
strings.term.DISCOVERY.body: The ways SalixTorrent can learn that other peers exist. Public torrents can use trackers, DHT, PEX and LPD/LAN. Private torrents intentionally restrict discovery to their configured trackers.
strings.term.DISCOVERY.title: Peer Discovery
strings.term.DISK_BACKPRESSURE.body: When the bounded write buffer is full, the peer coroutine that completed another piece sleeps on an asynchronous condition until the disk worker frees capacity. Other peers, Dear PyGui, trackers and timers remain runnable. Backpressure is therefore flow control, not a blocking busy-wait or polling loop.
strings.term.DISK_BACKPRESSURE.title: Disk Backpressure
strings.term.DISK_IO_PIPELINE.body: SalixTorrent writes newly verified pieces through one bounded write-behind queue instead of making a peer/network coroutine wait for synchronous filesystem I/O. The disk worker sleeps when idle and performs writes away from the event loop. Torrent completion is not announced until queued verified pieces are persisted.
strings.term.DISK_IO_PIPELINE.title: Asynchronous Disk I/O Pipeline
strings.term.DISK_TELEMETRY.body: Cached counters describing the disk pipeline: pending bytes/writes, write latency, completed/failed writes, backpressure events and time, plus recent-piece cache usage/hits/misses. Reading these values is O(1); SalixTorrent does not scan files or piece lists merely to update the display.
strings.term.DISK_TELEMETRY.title: Disk I/O Telemetry
strings.term.DISK_WRITE_BUFFER.body: A byte-limited queue of verified pieces waiting to be written to storage. The default limit is 64 MiB (or one full piece when a torrent uses unusually larger pieces). The bound prevents a fast network from creating unlimited Python memory growth when storage is slower than the incoming transfer.
strings.term.DISK_WRITE_BUFFER.title: Bounded Disk Write Buffer
strings.term.DOCUMENTATION_SCALE.body: Controls the semantic text scale used by the built-in Help and Glossary without changing the rest of SalixTorrent. Page titles, section headings, body text, captions and code keep their relative hierarchy while scaling together. The documentation renderer uses pre-registered scalable fonts, so changing this setting does not rebuild the font atlas while the application is running.
strings.term.DOCUMENTATION_SCALE.title: Documentation Text Scale
strings.term.DOCUMENTATION_SYSTEM.body: SalixTorrent's built-in manual is rendered from semantic document components rather than hard-coded widget formatting. A document describes titles, sections, paragraphs, callouts, links and media; the Dear PyGui renderer applies typography, readable line width, parent-relative anchoring and responsive reflow. This separation is designed for later extraction into a reusable application framework.
strings.term.DOCUMENTATION_SYSTEM.title: Documentation Subsystem
strings.term.DOCUMENT_CONTENT_BOUNDS.body: The parent-relative rectangle allocated to readable document content. On wide windows the manual keeps a bounded line length and centers that readable region inside the Help pane; on narrow windows it uses the available width. Centering therefore means center within the current document container, not center of the operating-system viewport.
strings.term.DOCUMENT_CONTENT_BOUNDS.title: Documentation Content Bounds
strings.term.DOCUMENT_LAYOUT_POLICY.body: The resolved geometry policy for a DocPage: maximum/minimum width, outer margins, inner padding, and document/title/media alignment. Framework defaults, sparse theme overrides and explicit page overrides resolve before current-window constraints are applied.
strings.term.DOCUMENT_LAYOUT_POLICY.title: Documentation Layout Policy
strings.term.DOCUMENT_MARGIN_PADDING.body: Margin is space outside the document rectangle, between the document and its parent pane. Padding is space inside that rectangle, between its edge and readable content. They are independent from title/media alignment, so changing content insets does not stop a title from centering within the current content bounds.
strings.term.DOCUMENT_MARGIN_PADDING.title: Documentation Margin and Padding
strings.term.DOCUMENT_MEDIA.body: Semantic media blocks let documentation refer to images, animation or video without tying the content model to a specific renderer. Static images are supported by the Dear PyGui documentation renderer now. Timed animation/video types are represented in the model and degrade to an explanatory fallback until a real decoder/player backend is implemented.
strings.term.DOCUMENT_MEDIA.title: Documentation Media
strings.term.DOUBLE_NAT.body: Two routing/NAT devices are in series, for example an ISP modem-router in front of a second home router. A port mapping on the inner router can succeed while the outer router still blocks unsolicited inbound traffic. Incoming Confirmed is stronger proof than a local mapping because it demonstrates the complete path in practice.
strings.term.DOUBLE_NAT.title: Double NAT
strings.term.DOWNLOADED.body: The verified payload data obtained for this torrent compared with its total size. For selective downloads, the completion state can also be based on only the files currently marked as wanted.
strings.term.DOWNLOADED.title: Downloaded
strings.term.DUAL_STACK.body: Using IPv4 and IPv6 at the same time. With Any interface selected, SalixTorrent opens explicit family-specific peer/DHT sockets when the operating system supports them. Selecting a specific IPv4 or IPv6 address constrains torrent networking to that family instead of silently escaping through the other one.
strings.term.DUAL_STACK.title: Dual Stack
strings.term.ELAPSED.body: How long this torrent has spent actively running in the current application session. Paused, stopped and queued time is excluded so the value is not mistaken for wall-clock age.
strings.term.ELAPSED.title: Active Time
strings.term.ENDGAME_MODE.body: A completion-latency strategy used only when a small tail of wanted blocks remains. SalixTorrent first assigns every still-unrequested tail block normally. If all remaining blocks are already outstanding, the oldest lingering requests may be duplicated to a bounded number of other peers. The first valid PIECE wins and SalixTorrent sends CANCEL to the other owners.
strings.term.ENDGAME_MODE.title: Endgame Mode
strings.term.ETA.body: An estimate of how long the currently wanted data will take to finish at the recent download rate. It changes naturally as peer availability and transfer speed change, and may be unavailable when speed is near zero.
strings.term.ETA.title: ETA - Estimated Time of Arrival
strings.term.EXIT_ON_COMPLETE.body: The --exit-on-complete headless option terminates after the wanted payload becomes complete. Without it, SalixTorrent remains alive and seeds until a shutdown signal is received.
strings.term.EXIT_ON_COMPLETE.title: Exit on Complete
strings.term.EXTERNAL_ADDRESS_SCOPE.body: How SalixTorrent classifies an external IPv4 address reported by a mapping protocol. Public means globally routable according to Python's IP address rules. Private, Shared/CGNAT, or other non-global values suggest an upstream NAT may still exist; this is a diagnostic clue rather than definitive proof of the ISP's network design.
strings.term.EXTERNAL_ADDRESS_SCOPE.title: External Address Scope
strings.term.EXTERNAL_ENDPOINT.body: The public Internet address/port reported by the router mapping system. It may be unavailable when no UPnP/NAT-PMP mapping exists, when the router does not reveal it, or when the network is behind CGNAT.
strings.term.EXTERNAL_ENDPOINT.title: External Endpoint
strings.term.FAST_RESUME.body: Saved verification state that lets SalixTorrent trust previously checked pieces after restart when the payload fingerprint still matches. If the files appear to have changed, SalixTorrent falls back to a full recheck.
strings.term.FAST_RESUME.title: Fast Resume
strings.term.FILE_COUNT.body: The number of payload files described by the torrent. A single-file torrent reports one file; a multi-file torrent preserves a relative directory tree of many payload files.
strings.term.FILE_COUNT.title: Torrent Files
strings.term.FILE_PIECES.body: The torrent-piece range that overlaps this file. BitTorrent piece boundaries do not have to align with file boundaries, so one piece can contain the end of one file and the beginning of the next.
strings.term.FILE_PIECES.title: File Piece Span
strings.term.FILE_PRIORITY.body: Controls which wanted files SalixTorrent tries to satisfy first. High outranks Normal, which outranks Low. Rarest-first selection is applied inside each priority level, so rarity never causes a Low-priority file to jump ahead of a wanted High-priority file. 'Don't Download' skips pieces used only by skipped files, while shared boundary pieces may still be needed.
strings.term.FILE_PRIORITY.title: Per-file Download Priority
strings.term.FILE_PROGRESS.body: The proportion of this file covered by SHA-1-verified torrent data. It is more meaningful than the file's current disk length because out-of-order downloads can create sparse or partially populated files.
strings.term.FILE_PROGRESS.title: Verified File Progress
strings.term.FILE_STATE.body: A summary derived from the verified and in-progress pieces that overlap this file. Because pieces can span file boundaries, the state reflects BitTorrent verification rather than only the physical file size on disk.
strings.term.FILE_STATE.title: File State
strings.term.FORCE_RECHECK.body: Discards SalixTorrent's fast-resume trust and SHA-1 verifies the existing payload again. It does not delete downloaded data. Use this if files were modified externally or you want to confirm on-disk data integrity.
strings.term.FORCE_RECHECK.title: Force Recheck
strings.term.GLOBAL_BANDWIDTH.body: A shared aggregate ceiling across every active torrent. For example, a 5 MB/s global download limit is shared by all downloads together; it is not 5 MB/s for each torrent. A value of 0 means unlimited.
strings.term.GLOBAL_BANDWIDTH.title: Global Bandwidth Limit
strings.term.HEADLESS_MODE.body: Runs SalixTorrent without Dear PyGui. Headless mode accepts v1/v2/hybrid .torrent files or compatible magnets, uses the same TorrentManager/peer/tracker/DHT engine as the desktop interface, and owns only terminal presentation and process lifecycle. Frozen Windows builds expose this path through SalixTorrentCLI.exe.
strings.term.HEADLESS_MODE.title: Headless Mode
strings.term.HEADLESS_STATUS.body: Rate-limited terminal presentation derived from structured TRANSFER_STATS and MAGNET events. The engine exposes state, progress, rates and peers; the CLI decides only how to render them.
strings.term.HEADLESS_STATUS.title: Headless Status Output
strings.term.HTTPS_TRACKER.body: A BitTorrent tracker contacted using encrypted HTTPS. It performs the same discovery role as an HTTP tracker while protecting the tracker request in transit. Torrent payload data is still exchanged peer-to-peer.
strings.term.HTTPS_TRACKER.title: HTTPS Tracker
strings.term.HTTP_TRACKER.body: A BitTorrent tracker contacted with HTTP announce requests for peer discovery. When its announce path has a standards-defined scrape counterpart, SalixTorrent can also batch BEP-48 scrape statistics for multiple active torrents. Torrent payload data does not pass through the tracker.
strings.term.HTTP_TRACKER.title: HTTP Tracker
strings.term.INCOMING_CONNECTIONS.body: Shows currently connected inbound peers and the number of successfully handshaken inbound peer connections observed during this application session. This is event-driven telemetry and does not require a polling loop.
strings.term.INCOMING_CONNECTIONS.title: Incoming Connections
strings.term.INFO_HASH.body: The SHA-1 identifier of a BitTorrent v1 torrent's exact bencoded info dictionary. Peers use it to identify the swarm, and v1 magnet links contain the same value as their btih identifier.
strings.term.INFO_HASH.title: Info Hash
strings.term.INTERFACE_LOCK.body: An active fail-closed guard for a specifically selected network address. Binding already chooses the source address; Interface Lock additionally monitors it. If that address disappears, SalixTorrent immediately moves the torrent to Error and closes its torrent networking instead of allowing a future connection to escape through another interface.
strings.term.INTERFACE_LOCK.title: Interface Lock / Kill Switch
strings.term.IPV6.body: The 128-bit Internet Protocol address family. SalixTorrent can connect to IPv6 peers, accept IPv6 peer TCP connections, consume tracker peers6 responses, exchange IPv6 PEX endpoints, and participate in BEP-32 DHT. IPv6 endpoints are displayed in brackets when a port follows them, for example [2001:db8::1]:6881.
strings.term.IPV6.title: IPv6
strings.term.IP_MASKING.body: A display-only privacy option that hides part of peer IP addresses in SalixTorrent's interface and peer table. It does not change the real socket address, hide you from the peer, tracker or ISP, or provide network anonymity. It is useful mainly when sharing screenshots or screen recordings.
strings.term.IP_MASKING.title: Peer IP Masking
strings.term.JSON_STATUS.body: The --json-status headless option emits one JSON object per line for scripts or supervisory tools. It uses the same structured engine events as human-readable status and does not import Dear PyGui.
strings.term.JSON_STATUS.title: JSON Status
strings.term.LAN.body: Your nearby private network, such as computers connected to the same home or office router. LAN peers can often exchange data directly at local-network speed without sending the payload through the Internet.
strings.term.LAN.title: LAN - Local Area Network
strings.term.LAST_INCOMING.body: The most recent remote BitTorrent peer observed connecting to SalixTorrent's listen socket. Seeing one is practical evidence that an inbound path is working from at least that peer's network location.
strings.term.LAST_INCOMING.title: Last Incoming Peer
strings.term.LAST_UPLOAD.body: How long ago this torrent last successfully transmitted a PIECE payload to a peer. An idle seed can correctly show no current upload speed even when this value proves that it served data recently.
strings.term.LAST_UPLOAD.title: Last Upload
strings.term.LISTENER_ENDPOINT.body: The exact local IPv4 address and TCP port used by the selected torrent's incoming peer listener. 0.0.0.0 means the socket accepts connections on all local IPv4 interfaces; a specific address means network binding is active.
strings.term.LISTENER_ENDPOINT.title: Listener Endpoint
strings.term.LISTEN_PORT.body: The TCP port on which SalixTorrent accepts incoming peer connections. SalixTorrent can try nearby fallback ports if the preferred port is already in use. DHT may use the same number over UDP.
strings.term.LISTEN_PORT.title: BitTorrent Listen Port
strings.term.LOCAL_ENDPOINT.body: The local address and listen port used by SalixTorrent, for example 192.168.x.x:6881 or [2001:db8::10]:6881. IPv4 private addresses are usually LAN-only; IPv6 scope depends on the selected address and network route.
strings.term.LOCAL_ENDPOINT.title: Local Endpoint
strings.term.LPD.body: BEP-14 Local Peer Discovery uses IPv4 multicast to find compatible peers on the same LAN. It does not search the wider Internet. Because BEP-14 is IPv4-multicast based, SalixTorrent disables LPD under an explicit IPv6-only bind rather than leaking discovery through a different IPv4 interface. Private torrents also disable LPD.
strings.term.LPD.title: LPD - Local Peer Discovery
strings.term.MAGNET_LINK.body: A compact URI that identifies a torrent by info hash without carrying the full .torrent metadata. SalixTorrent discovers peers, retrieves metadata with BEP-9, verifies the hash, then turns it into an ordinary torrent session.
strings.term.MAGNET_LINK.title: Magnet Link
strings.term.MAGNET_URI_REGISTRATION.body: Windows URL-protocol registration used when clicking magnet links. Because the scheme has one active owner, SalixTorrent makes this opt-in and restores a captured previous handler only when safe.
strings.term.MAGNET_URI_REGISTRATION.title: magnet: URI Registration
strings.term.MANUAL_PORT_FORWARD.body: A router rule configured by the user that sends unsolicited Internet traffic on a chosen external port to SalixTorrent's local computer and listen port. TCP is the important mapping for incoming BitTorrent peers; forwarding the same UDP port can also improve DHT reachability. The computer should keep a stable LAN address/reservation.
strings.term.MANUAL_PORT_FORWARD.title: Manual Port Forward
strings.term.MAPPED_PROTOCOLS.body: TCP mapping is used for incoming BitTorrent peer connections. UDP mapping can help DHT reachability. A mapping only means the router accepted the rule; a real incoming peer is stronger proof that connectivity works.
strings.term.MAPPED_PROTOCOLS.title: Mapped Protocols
strings.term.MAPPING_DIAGNOSIS.body: A cached explanation derived from the most recent UPnP/NAT-PMP attempt for the selected listen port. It distinguishes discovery failure, gateway refusal, port conflicts, malformed replies and other mapping stages. The diagnosis is updated when mapping work already occurs; SalixTorrent does not continuously poll the router.
strings.term.MAPPING_DIAGNOSIS.title: Incoming Connectivity Diagnosis
strings.term.MAPPING_LEASE.body: Automatic router mappings can have finite lifetimes. SalixTorrent keeps one low-frequency renewal timer for all active mapped listen ports and refreshes finite leases before expiry. If a UPnP gateway requires a permanent lease, SalixTorrent records that fact and does not schedule unnecessary renewals. It does not run a polling loop per torrent.
strings.term.MAPPING_LEASE.title: Port Mapping Lease Refresh
strings.term.MAPPING_METHOD_STATUS.body: Shows UPnP and NAT-PMP separately so an Unmapped result explains which method failed, was disabled, or was not needed. UPnP is attempted first; NAT-PMP is the fallback when enabled.
strings.term.MAPPING_METHOD_STATUS.title: Port Mapping Method Status
strings.term.MAX_PEERS.body: The default connection target used for torrents added later. More peers can improve source diversity but also consume sockets, memory, CPU and bandwidth. Existing torrents keep the values already assigned to them.
strings.term.MAX_PEERS.title: Default Maximum Peers
strings.term.MERKLE_TREE.body: A binary hash tree where parent hashes authenticate child hashes. BitTorrent v2 uses SHA-256 Merkle trees per file, allowing piece/block data to be proven against a trusted pieces root without storing a flat SHA-1 hash list in the v2 metadata.
strings.term.MERKLE_TREE.title: Merkle Tree
strings.term.MINIMIZE_TRAY.body: When the active tray and native window-control backend are both healthy, minimizing hides the main window while transfers continue. SalixTorrent will not hide itself if it cannot prove that a live tray can restore the window.
strings.term.MINIMIZE_TRAY.title: Minimize to System Tray
strings.term.MSE.body: A legacy BitTorrent peer-transport encryption/obfuscation mechanism. SalixTorrent negotiates MSE with Diffie-Hellman and protects the peer-wire stream with RC4 after discarding the first 1024 keystream bytes. It can make simple protocol inspection harder, but it is not modern authenticated encryption, does not provide anonymity, and cannot guarantee that an ISP cannot identify or block BitTorrent traffic.
strings.term.MSE.title: MSE - Message Stream Encryption
strings.term.NATIVE_NOTIFICATION.body: Uses the active desktop notification capability to announce completed downloads outside the main SalixTorrent window. Windows uses the notification-area backend; Linux/BSD and macOS can use their available desktop notification service. Notification capability is independent from torrent networking.
strings.term.NATIVE_NOTIFICATION.title: Native Desktop Completion Notification
strings.term.NATPMP.body: A lightweight automatic router port-mapping protocol used as a fallback when UPnP is unavailable. SalixTorrent decodes standard NAT-PMP result codes so a timeout, authorization refusal, network failure, resource exhaustion, or unsupported operation can be distinguished. Failure remains non-fatal to outbound transfers.
strings.term.NATPMP.title: NAT-PMP - NAT Port Mapping Protocol
strings.term.NETWORK_BINDING.body: Pins SalixTorrent torrent networking to a selected local IPv4 or IPv6 address. Peer TCP connections and listeners, HTTP/UDP trackers, DHT and magnet metadata retrieval use that source family/address. BEP-14 LPD is IPv4-only and therefore stays disabled under an explicit IPv6 bind. Choosing Any interface permits dual-stack system routing where supported.
strings.term.NETWORK_BINDING.title: Network Interface / VPN Binding
strings.term.NEW_TORRENT_LIMITS.body: Per-torrent upload/download limits copied onto torrents added in the future. Changing these defaults does not overwrite custom limits already stored on existing torrents.
strings.term.NEW_TORRENT_LIMITS.title: New Torrent Default Limits
strings.term.OPEN_FOLDER.body: Opens the filesystem location containing this torrent's payload. This does not pause or modify the torrent. Editing/deleting payload files externally can cause a later recheck to mark pieces missing or corrupt.
strings.term.OPEN_FOLDER.title: Open Download Folder
strings.term.OPEN_MAGNET.body: Paste a compatible btih, btmh or hybrid magnet URI. SalixTorrent resolves the missing metainfo through compatible peers, verifies the advertised identity and any required v2 piece layers, then creates the normal persistent torrent session.
strings.term.OPEN_MAGNET.title: Open Magnet
strings.term.OPEN_TORRENT.body: Choose a .torrent metainfo file, add it to SalixTorrent, select it, and start its normal checking/download workflow. The .torrent contains metadata; the payload is downloaded separately into its storage path.
strings.term.OPEN_TORRENT.title: Open Torrent
strings.term.OUTSTANDING_REQUEST.body: A block that SalixTorrent has assigned to a particular peer but has not yet received. Normal downloading gives a block one owner. During endgame a small number of peers may temporarily own the same final block; ownership is cleared when data arrives, a peer disconnects/chokes, or the request times out.
strings.term.OUTSTANDING_REQUEST.title: Outstanding Block Request
strings.term.PAUSE_TORRENT.body: Temporarily suspends active transfer work while keeping the torrent loaded and preserving its intended resumable state. Use Stop when you want it to remain inactive until explicitly started again.
strings.term.PAUSE_TORRENT.title: Pause Torrent
strings.term.PE.body: A common BitTorrent name for the same family of encrypted/obfuscated peer transport negotiated by MSE. In SalixTorrent, an encrypted peer shown as MSE/RC4 is using this transport; tracker HTTPS is a separate security layer.
strings.term.PE.title: PE - Protocol Encryption
strings.term.PEER_ADDRESS.body: The remote IP address and TCP port of this live BitTorrent connection. It identifies the network endpoint SalixTorrent is talking to, not the person or account using that client. Optional IP masking changes only how the address is displayed in SalixTorrent; the real endpoint is still required for the peer-to-peer connection.
strings.term.PEER_ADDRESS.title: Peer Address
strings.term.PEER_AGE.body: How long this particular peer connection has remained established during the current torrent run. Disconnecting and reconnecting starts a new age.
strings.term.PEER_AGE.title: Connection Age
strings.term.PEER_CLIENT.body: A best-effort client name/version decoded from the peer ID or extension handshake sent by the remote program. It is self-reported protocol information and is not cryptographic proof of the remote software.
strings.term.PEER_CLIENT.title: Peer Client
strings.term.PEER_DIRECTION.body: Outgoing means SalixTorrent initiated the TCP connection. Incoming means the remote peer connected to SalixTorrent's listen port. Either direction can carry both downloads and uploads.
strings.term.PEER_DIRECTION.title: Connection Direction
strings.term.PEER_ENCRYPTION_POLICY.body: Disabled uses normal plaintext BitTorrent peer transport. Prefer Encryption tries MSE/RC4 first and, if the peer does not support it, opens a fresh plaintext TCP connection. Require Encryption accepts only MSE/RC4 peer transport and never falls back to plaintext.
strings.term.PEER_ENCRYPTION_POLICY.title: Peer Encryption Policy
strings.term.PEER_FLAGS.body: I = SalixTorrent is interested in data from the peer; i = the peer is interested in our data; C = the peer is choking us; c = we are choking the peer. Choking is normal BitTorrent flow control, not an error.
strings.term.PEER_FLAGS.title: Peer Protocol Flags
strings.term.PEER_PROGRESS.body: An estimate of how much of the torrent this remote peer has advertised through its bitfield and HAVE messages. '--' means the peer has not sent enough information to calculate a percentage.
strings.term.PEER_PROGRESS.title: Peer Piece Completion
strings.term.PEER_SOURCE.body: How SalixTorrent originally learned about this peer: a tracker, DHT, PEX, Local Peer Discovery, or an incoming connection. The data connection itself is still a direct peer-to-peer TCP connection.
strings.term.PEER_SOURCE.title: Peer Source
strings.term.PEER_STATE.body: A compact summary of what this connection is doing now, such as Ready, Downloading, Uploading, or Choked. The peer-wire flags provide the more precise protocol-level flow-control state.
strings.term.PEER_STATE.title: Peer Connection State
strings.term.PEX.body: A BitTorrent extension where already-connected peers introduce one another to additional peers. SalixTorrent negotiates BEP-10 and exchanges BEP-11 IPv4 added/dropped endpoints plus IPv6 added6/dropped6 endpoints. Private torrents deliberately disable PEX.
strings.term.PEX.title: PEX - Peer Exchange
strings.term.PIECE.body: A torrent payload is divided into fixed-size pieces. Each piece has a cryptographic hash and is treated as trusted only after the complete piece has been received and verified.
strings.term.PIECE.title: Torrent Pieces
strings.term.PIECES_ROOT.body: A 32-byte SHA-256 Merkle root describing one non-empty file in a BEP-52 torrent. The tree is built from 16 KiB leaf blocks; missing leaves needed only to balance the tree use deterministic zero-subtree hashes.
strings.term.PIECES_ROOT.title: Pieces Root
strings.term.PIECE_AVAILABILITY.body: How many currently connected peers advertise that they possess this specific piece. SalixTorrent updates this count incrementally from peer BITFIELD, HAVE, and disconnect events and uses it for rarest-first piece selection. A value of 0 means no connected peer is currently known to supply the piece.
strings.term.PIECE_AVAILABILITY.title: Piece Availability
strings.term.PIECE_LAYERS_V2.body: A top-level metainfo dictionary mapping a file's pieces root to concatenated 32-byte hashes at the layer where each hash covers one configured torrent piece. SalixTorrent verifies the expected count and reconstructs the declared root instead of trusting the layer as opaque metadata.
strings.term.PIECE_LAYERS_V2.title: BEP-52 Piece Layers
strings.term.PIECE_MAP.body: A visual overview of the torrent's piece states. Large torrents are condensed so one map cell can represent several pieces. The map is a display aid only; verification still happens per real torrent piece.
strings.term.PIECE_MAP.title: Piece Map
strings.term.PIECE_SIZE.body: The amount of payload represented by most torrent pieces. Smaller pieces create more hashes and metadata but allow finer-grained verification; larger pieces reduce metadata overhead. The final piece may be smaller.
strings.term.PIECE_SIZE.title: Piece Size
strings.term.PIECE_STATE.body: Verified means the piece hash passed. Downloading/Requested means work is in progress. Missing means it is still needed. No known source means it is needed but no currently connected peer advertises it.
strings.term.PIECE_STATE.title: Piece State
strings.term.PORTABLE_MODE.body: Activated by portable.flag beside the executable or --portable for one launch. Writable state uses a data folder beside the executable and a new profile defaults downloads beside it.
strings.term.PORTABLE_MODE.title: Portable Mode
strings.term.PORT_MAPPING.body: An IPv4 NAT-router rule forwarding an Internet-facing port to one of SalixTorrent's active listen sockets. UPnP/NAT-PMP are not required for globally routed IPv6; an IPv6 listener instead depends on the route and host/router firewall allowing inbound traffic. Multiple IPv4 listener mappings remain independent.
strings.term.PORT_MAPPING.title: Incoming Port Mapping
strings.term.PREFERENCES_VIEW.body: Persistent SalixTorrent settings for storage defaults, peer encryption, network-interface/VPN binding, Interface Lock, peer-IP display masking, discovery, queue behavior, bandwidth, transfer-rate display and desktop integration.
strings.term.PREFERENCES_VIEW.title: Preferences
strings.term.PRIVATE_TORRENT.body: A torrent marked private restricts swarm discovery to its configured trackers. SalixTorrent disables DHT, PEX, Local Peer Discovery and public fallback trackers to avoid leaking the private swarm's info hash.
strings.term.PRIVATE_TORRENT.title: Private Torrent
strings.term.PROPERTIES.body: Opens a consolidated readout of torrent metadata, paths, trackers, transfer statistics, priority, and limits for the selected torrent.
strings.term.PROPERTIES.title: Torrent Properties
strings.term.PROPERTY_CASCADE.body: The deterministic configuration order used by reusable presentation primitives: a safe framework Default is optionally overridden by a valid Theme value, then by a valid explicit Instance value. Invalid higher-precedence candidates fall back one layer at a time instead of breaking the component or replacing unrelated properties.
strings.term.PROPERTY_CASCADE.title: Framework Property Cascade
strings.term.QUEUE_ORDER.body: The persistent scheduling order controlled by Move Up / Move Down. Within the same priority level, torrents earlier in this order are considered first when a download slot becomes available.
strings.term.QUEUE_ORDER.title: Queue Order
strings.term.QUEUE_PRIORITY.body: High, Normal, or Low scheduling importance for a torrent. Priority is considered before queue position when a download slot becomes available. Changing display sorting does not change this scheduling priority.
strings.term.QUEUE_PRIORITY.title: Torrent Queue Priority
strings.term.QUEUE_SEARCH.body: Filters the visible transfer list by torrent name. It does not stop, remove, reprioritize, or otherwise change hidden torrents.
strings.term.QUEUE_SEARCH.title: Torrent Search Filter
strings.term.QUEUE_SORT.body: Click a column header to sort what you see. Sorting is visual only and does not alter the real Move Up / Move Down queue order or scheduler priority. Use Queue Order to return to scheduling order.
strings.term.QUEUE_SORT.title: Display Sorting
strings.term.QUEUE_STATUS_FILTER.body: Shows only torrents in the chosen lifecycle state (or Active group). This is a display filter only; hidden torrents keep running according to their normal queue and transfer state.
strings.term.QUEUE_STATUS_FILTER.title: Status Filter
strings.term.RANDOM_TIE_BREAKING.body: When several wanted pieces have the same file priority and the same peer availability, SalixTorrent chooses between them randomly instead of always starting at the lowest piece number. This avoids deterministic piece-order clustering between clients while preserving rarest-first behaviour.
strings.term.RANDOM_TIE_BREAKING.title: Random Rarity Tie-Breaking
strings.term.RAREST_FIRST.body: Within the current file-priority level, SalixTorrent prefers incomplete pieces advertised by the fewest connected peers. Acquiring scarce pieces early reduces the chance of losing access to them and helps redistribute rare data through the swarm. File priority remains the stronger rule.
strings.term.RAREST_FIRST.title: Rarest-First Piece Selection
strings.term.RC4.body: The legacy stream cipher used by BitTorrent MSE/PE. SalixTorrent uses the MSE RC4-drop1024 convention required for interoperability. RC4 should not be confused with modern authenticated encryption and is used here only because it is part of the legacy peer-encryption protocol.
strings.term.RC4.title: RC4
strings.term.RECENT_PIECE_CACHE.body: A bounded in-memory LRU cache for pieces that were just verified and written. It lets upload requests reuse hot piece data instead of immediately reading it back from disk. A verified piece that is still waiting in the write buffer is also served from its pinned memory copy, so write-behind never creates an upload gap.
strings.term.RECENT_PIECE_CACHE.title: Recent-Piece Read Cache
strings.term.REMAINING.body: The amount of currently wanted torrent data that is not yet verified. Changing file priorities or marking files 'Don't Download' can change the amount considered remaining.
strings.term.REMAINING.title: Remaining
strings.term.REMOVE_TORRENT.body: Removes the transfer from SalixTorrent's queue/session state. The safe remove option leaves payload data on disk; the separate Delete Data option also removes SalixTorrent-managed payload/resume data after confirmation.
strings.term.REMOVE_TORRENT.title: Remove Torrent
strings.term.REQUEST_PIPELINE.body: Keeping several 16 KiB REQUEST messages outstanding to one unchoked peer so network round-trip latency does not leave the connection idle between blocks. SalixTorrent adapts the target depth from observed peer throughput and clamps it to a strict per-peer range, preventing an unresponsive peer from owning an unbounded amount of work.
strings.term.REQUEST_PIPELINE.title: Request Pipelining
strings.term.REQUEST_SCHEDULER.body: The block-level scheduler that turns rarest-first piece choices into bounded peer-wire REQUEST pipelines. SalixTorrent tracks exactly which peer owns each outstanding block, expires stalled ownership for reassignment, and activates bounded duplicate requests only during endgame. The scheduler is event-driven; it does not rescan the entire torrent on every peer message.
strings.term.REQUEST_SCHEDULER.title: Download Request Scheduler
strings.term.REQUEST_TIMEOUT.body: A deadline applied after a REQUEST frame is actually transmitted. If the peer does not return that block before the deadline, SalixTorrent releases the peer's ownership and the scheduler can immediately assign the block elsewhere. A CANCEL is also sent to the stale peer when the connection is still alive.
strings.term.REQUEST_TIMEOUT.title: Block Request Timeout
strings.term.RESPONSIVE_LAYOUT.body: SalixTorrent's workspace and data-rich dialogs respond to actual resize events rather than polling geometry every frame. Expandable regions consume available space, text wrapping follows the rendered pane width, and dialog action rows remain attached to their content boundary. Small destructive confirmations and transient notices can remain intentionally fixed-size, matching normal desktop-application conventions.
strings.term.RESPONSIVE_LAYOUT.title: Responsive Interface Layout
strings.term.RETRY_TORRENT.body: Attempts to restart a torrent after an error or recoverable problem. The original human-readable error remains useful for understanding what failed before retrying.
strings.term.RETRY_TORRENT.title: Retry Torrent
strings.term.SCRAPE_BATCHING.body: Instead of sending one scrape request per torrent, SalixTorrent groups active torrents that use the same tracker. HTTP requests carry repeated info_hash parameters in bounded batches; UDP requests carry many 20-byte info hashes under one tracker connection. The coordinator is shared application-wide and timer-driven, so the UI does not create network traffic merely by displaying statistics.
strings.term.SCRAPE_BATCHING.title: Tracker Scrape Batching
strings.term.SCRAPE_COMPLETED.body: The C value from a tracker scrape is the tracker's cumulative count of completed downloads for that info hash. It is not the number of current seeds and it is not a globally authoritative total: different trackers may maintain different populations and historical counters.
strings.term.SCRAPE_COMPLETED.title: Scrape Completed Downloads
strings.term.SEEDS_LEECHERS.body: A seed has the complete torrent and can upload any piece. A leecher is still obtaining some of the torrent. Tracker counts are estimates and can differ from SalixTorrent's currently connected peers.
strings.term.SEEDS_LEECHERS.title: Seeds / Leechers
strings.term.SESSION_STATE.body: The current internal lifecycle state for this torrent. It controls which network, checking, disk, and peer-worker activities are currently active.
strings.term.SESSION_STATE.title: Session State
strings.term.SETTINGS_FILE.body: The JSON file containing persistent application preferences. It is kept in SalixTorrent's application-data directory rather than mixed with torrent payloads.
strings.term.SETTINGS_FILE.title: Settings File
strings.term.SHARE_RATIO.body: Uploaded payload divided by downloaded payload. A ratio of 1.0 means roughly as much data has been uploaded as downloaded. A source-backed seed can upload even though SalixTorrent itself downloaded zero bytes.
strings.term.SHARE_RATIO.title: Share Ratio
strings.term.SOURCE_DETAIL.body: Protocol-specific diagnostic information such as tracker announce intervals, DHT node activity, PEX receive/transmit counts, or the Local Peer Discovery multicast endpoint.
strings.term.SOURCE_DETAIL.title: Discovery Detail
strings.term.SOURCE_LAST_UPDATE.body: How long ago SalixTorrent last received or recorded activity from this discovery source. 'Never' means no result has been recorded yet.
strings.term.SOURCE_LAST_UPDATE.title: Last Discovery Update
strings.term.SOURCE_PEERS.body: This count belongs to one discovery source and is not necessarily the number of peers currently connected. Sources can discover duplicate, offline, unreachable, or already-connected endpoints.
strings.term.SOURCE_PEERS.title: Peers Reported by This Source
strings.term.SOURCE_RESPONSE.body: How long the latest tracker request took to complete. This measures the tracker response, not a peer's download latency or transfer speed. '--' means this source does not expose a comparable request/response time.
strings.term.SOURCE_RESPONSE.title: Discovery Response Time
strings.term.SOURCE_WAITING.body: A neutral discovery state. The source exists but has not produced a result yet, or its next scheduled announce/query has not run. Waiting is not a failure and does not imply that the torrent is unable to find peers through other sources.
strings.term.SOURCE_WAITING.title: Discovery Source: Waiting
strings.term.SPEED_HISTORY.body: A short in-memory history of the selected torrent's measured download and upload rates. It is sampled about every half second and intentionally resets when SalixTorrent restarts rather than bloating session storage.
strings.term.SPEED_HISTORY.title: Rolling Transfer History
strings.term.SPEED_WINDOW.body: Chooses how much recent transfer history is visible on the Speed graph. Changing the window affects only the visualization; it does not change sampling, bandwidth limits, or transfer behavior.
strings.term.SPEED_WINDOW.title: Graph Time Window
strings.term.STANDALONE_BUILD.body: A frozen SalixTorrent executable containing the Python runtime and application dependencies. The desktop build is windowed; SalixTorrentCLI.exe keeps console/headless behavior separate.
strings.term.STANDALONE_BUILD.title: Standalone Build
strings.term.START_RESUME.body: Starts a stopped/completed/error torrent or resumes a paused one. If the download-slot limit is already full, the torrent can wait in Queued state until a slot becomes available.
strings.term.START_RESUME.title: Start / Resume Torrent
strings.term.START_SEEDING.body: Adds the newly created torrent to Active Transfers and seeds directly from the original source path after verifying it. SalixTorrent does not make an unnecessary duplicate copy inside the downloads directory.
strings.term.START_SEEDING.title: Start Seeding Created Torrent
strings.term.STOP_TORRENT.body: Stops active transfer/checking work and records the torrent as intentionally stopped. Downloaded payload and verified resume state remain on disk.
strings.term.STOP_TORRENT.title: Stop Torrent
strings.term.STORAGE_MODE.body: Downloads are written to SalixTorrent-managed storage. 'External Seed' means SalixTorrent is reading an already-complete original file/folder in place and treats that source as read-only.
strings.term.STORAGE_MODE.title: Storage Mode
strings.term.STORAGE_PATH.body: The filesystem path containing this torrent's payload data. Opening the folder does not alter transfer state; changing or deleting data externally can invalidate fast-resume information and require a recheck.
strings.term.STORAGE_PATH.title: Storage Path
strings.term.STORAGE_ROOT.body: The directory or external source backing this torrent's payload. Normal downloads write under the configured download directory. External seeds are read-only and are served directly from their original location.
strings.term.STORAGE_ROOT.title: Storage Root
strings.term.SWARM_HEALTH.body: A human-readable summary derived from the torrent's current peer and piece availability. It helps explain whether the connected swarm appears capable of supplying the wanted data; it is not a guarantee of speed.
strings.term.SWARM_HEALTH.title: Swarm Health
strings.term.SWARM_SL.body: Seed/leecher counts reported by a tracker announce result. The Sources view keeps these announce figures separate from scrape S/L/C statistics so advanced users can see which tracker operation supplied each number. '--' means the source has not provided comparable announce counts.
strings.term.SWARM_SL.title: Swarm S/L - Seeds / Leechers
strings.term.SYSTEM_TRAY.body: Creates the platform's supported background icon: the Windows notification area, a Linux/BSD tray backend, or the macOS menu bar. The backend publishes Open, Pause All, Resume All and Exit when its menu implementation supports those actions. Diagnostics reports the selected backend and limitations.
strings.term.SYSTEM_TRAY.title: System Tray / Menu Bar Integration
strings.term.TCP.body: The reliable, connection-oriented transport used for normal BitTorrent peer-wire connections. One TCP peer connection is bidirectional: both clients can upload and download pieces over the same connection.
strings.term.TCP.title: TCP - Transmission Control Protocol
strings.term.TORRENT_COMMENT.body: Optional human-readable metadata stored in the .torrent file. It does not affect piece hashes, transfer behavior, or the torrent's info hash unless placed inside the info dictionary (SalixTorrent stores it outside).
strings.term.TORRENT_COMMENT.title: Torrent Comment
strings.term.TORRENT_FILE_ASSOCIATION.body: Windows per-user registration advertising SalixTorrent as an Open With handler through its own ProgID. It does not silently overwrite another torrent client's default application choice.
strings.term.TORRENT_FILE_ASSOCIATION.title: .torrent File Association
strings.term.TORRENT_GENERATION.body: Selects the metainfo produced by Create Torrent. Hybrid v1/v2 is recommended for broad compatibility and contains both SHA-1 and SHA-256 identities with BEP-47 padding for v1 alignment. BitTorrent v1 and BitTorrent v2 create single-generation torrents.
strings.term.TORRENT_GENERATION.title: Torrent Generation
strings.term.TORRENT_IDENTITY_V2.body: For meta version 2, the exact bencoded info dictionary is hashed with SHA-256. SalixTorrent stores the full 32-byte identity and only derives the 20-byte truncated form where BEP-52 explicitly requires a tracker/peer-wire identifier.
strings.term.TORRENT_IDENTITY_V2.title: v2 SHA-256 Torrent Identity
strings.term.TORRENT_OUTPUT.body: Where the generated .torrent metadata file will be saved. This file is small compared with the payload and can be shared independently; it contains metadata and piece hashes, not the original payload data.
strings.term.TORRENT_OUTPUT.title: Torrent Output File
strings.term.TORRENT_PATH.body: The local .torrent metainfo file used to reconstruct this session. SalixTorrent also keeps private cached metadata so restored sessions are not dependent on the originally opened .torrent file remaining in place.
strings.term.TORRENT_PATH.title: .torrent Metadata Path
strings.term.TORRENT_PROTOCOL_POLICY.body: Controls which compatible swarm generation a transfer may use. Auto / Best Compatible uses v1 for v1 torrents, v2 for v2 torrents, and both swarms for hybrid torrents. The v1 Only and v2 Only choices are advanced compatibility/debugging overrides; they cannot invent a generation that the torrent does not contain.
strings.term.TORRENT_PROTOCOL_POLICY.title: Torrent Protocol Policy
strings.term.TORRENT_SOURCE_FILE.body: Select one existing file to publish as a single-file torrent. Archives, disk images, videos and ordinary files are all treated as normal payload bytes; SalixTorrent does not interpret their internal format.
strings.term.TORRENT_SOURCE_FILE.title: Single-file Torrent Source
strings.term.TORRENT_SOURCE_FOLDER.body: Select a directory to create a multi-file torrent preserving its relative file tree. Directory symlinks are deliberately not followed so creation does not unexpectedly include data outside the selected folder.
strings.term.TORRENT_SOURCE_FOLDER.title: Multi-file Torrent Source
strings.term.TORRENT_STATUS.body: The selected torrent's current lifecycle state, such as Checking, Queued, Downloading, Paused, Seeding, Stopped, Completed, or Error.
strings.term.TORRENT_STATUS.title: Torrent Status
strings.term.TRACKER.body: A server that introduces peers participating in the same torrent. The tracker coordinates discovery; the actual torrent payload is transferred directly between peers, not through the tracker.
strings.term.TRACKER.title: BitTorrent Tracker
strings.term.TRACKER_LIST.body: Tracker announce URLs embedded in the .torrent metadata. Other clients can contact these servers to discover peers. One URL is entered per line; blank/comment lines are ignored and duplicates are removed.
strings.term.TRACKER_LIST.title: Tracker List
strings.term.TRACKER_SCRAPE.body: A tracker scrape asks for swarm statistics without announcing SalixTorrent as a peer and without changing swarm participation. S is complete peers (seeds), L is incomplete peers (leechers), and C is the tracker's cumulative completed-download counter. SalixTorrent batches multiple active torrents that share a tracker so one scrape can return several swarms' statistics efficiently. HTTP uses the BEP-48 scrape endpoint; UDP uses BEP-15 action 2.
strings.term.TRACKER_SCRAPE.title: Tracker Scrape - S / L / C
strings.term.TRACKER_TIMEOUT.body: A warning that one tracker did not answer before its request deadline. Public trackers can be overloaded, offline, filtered, or temporarily unreachable. A timeout is source-local rather than a torrent failure: other trackers, DHT, PEX and LPD can continue discovering peers, and already-connected peers are unaffected.
strings.term.TRACKER_TIMEOUT.title: Tracker Timeout
strings.term.TRANSFER_ADD_API.body: The presentation-neutral path used by desktop Open Torrent/Open Magnet, startup targets and headless inputs. A TransferAddRequest carries source and policy; TorrentManager performs the actual validation, magnet resolution, session creation and optional start operation.
strings.term.TRANSFER_ADD_API.title: Shared Transfer-Add API
strings.term.TRANSFER_LIMITS.body: Optional speed ceilings that apply only to the selected torrent. A value of 0 means unlimited. These work alongside the application-wide global bandwidth limits in Preferences.
strings.term.TRANSFER_LIMITS.title: Per-torrent Transfer Limits
strings.term.TRANSFER_RATE.body: Controls how live upload/download speeds are displayed. KB/s and MB/s show bytes per second; kbps and Mbps show bits per second. This changes presentation only and does not change limits or network speed.
strings.term.TRANSFER_RATE.title: Transfer Rate Units
strings.term.TRANSPORT_SECURITY.body: Shows how a live BitTorrent peer connection is carrying the peer-wire stream. MSE/RC4 means peer transport encryption was negotiated; Plaintext means the normal unencrypted peer stream is in use. This describes the peer connection only, not tracker HTTPS, VPN tunnelling, or anonymity.
strings.term.TRANSPORT_SECURITY.title: Transport Security
strings.term.UDP.body: A lightweight datagram transport used by DHT, UDP trackers, Local Peer Discovery multicast, and some automatic router-mapping protocols. UDP does not establish a reliable stream like TCP does.
strings.term.UDP.title: UDP - User Datagram Protocol
strings.term.UDP_TRACKER.body: A tracker using BEP-15's compact UDP protocol. In addition to announce, BEP-15 defines a scrape action that can return seed, leecher and completed-download counts for many info hashes in one datagram. Torrent payload is still exchanged directly between peers.
strings.term.UDP_TRACKER.title: UDP Tracker
strings.term.UI_TEXT_SIZE.body: Controls the font size used throughout SalixTorrent, including menus, tables, tooltips, Preferences and Help Topics. Comfortable (15 px) is the default. Larger sizes are useful on high-density or physically smaller displays. SalixTorrent prefers a scalable system monospace font so text remains crisp instead of enlarging Dear PyGui's tiny bitmap font.
strings.term.UI_TEXT_SIZE.title: Interface Text Size
strings.term.UNSET_INHERITANCE.body: A framework sentinel meaning that an instance or sparse theme did not provide a value and should inherit the next lower-precedence layer. It is intentionally distinct from None, which can remain an explicit semantic value such as no configured maximum document width.
strings.term.UNSET_INHERITANCE.title: UNSET Inheritance
strings.term.UPDATE_TRACKERS.body: Requests an immediate tracker announce for the selected active torrent instead of waiting for the next normal announce interval. Newly returned peer addresses are fed into the running swarm.
strings.term.UPDATE_TRACKERS.title: Update / Announce Trackers
strings.term.UPLOADED.body: The persisted cumulative payload bytes SalixTorrent has served to other peers for this torrent. Uploading can happen while downloading as soon as verified pieces are available and continues naturally while seeding.
strings.term.UPLOADED.title: Uploaded Total
strings.term.UPLOADED_SESSION.body: Payload bytes served by this torrent since the current SalixTorrent process created/restored the torrent session. This counter is intentionally lightweight and is not persisted across application restarts.
strings.term.UPLOADED_SESSION.title: Uploaded This Session
strings.term.UPLOAD_REQUESTS.body: Counts BitTorrent REQUEST messages received and how many were successfully served with PIECE payload data. The counters update only when those network events happen; SalixTorrent does not scan peers to calculate them.
strings.term.UPLOAD_REQUESTS.title: Upload Requests
strings.term.UPNP.body: A router protocol SalixTorrent can use to request automatic incoming port mappings for its active torrent listeners. SalixTorrent records the exact stage and router fault code when available, and automatically retries with a permanent lease when an IGD reports that only permanent mappings are supported. Failure is not fatal: outbound peer connections can still download and upload normally.
strings.term.UPNP.title: UPnP - Universal Plug and Play
strings.term.VPN.body: A network path provided by VPN software, usually exposed to applications as a local interface/address. Selecting that address in Network Interface / VPN Binding pins SalixTorrent torrent traffic to it; Interface Lock adds active fail-closed monitoring if the address vanishes.
strings.term.VPN.title: VPN - Virtual Private Network
